subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-19 (kb/Work PB568). The PARTIAL was not about the SR10 predicate, which was always right, but about REACHABILITY: character-string-1's character-1 is written BARE in the printed general format - re-rendered here from the canonical PDF at printed page 441, PDF page 471: `EDITING character-1 { IS literal-1 | FOR { NEGATIVE IS literal-2 | POSITIVE IS literal-3 } }`, character-1 carrying no quotation marks and named character-1 exactly as character-string-1 is, while literal-1/-2/-3 are named as literals. CobolData.g4's editingPhrase demanded a quoted literal there, so every CONFORMING EDITING phrase was a parse error and SR10 was reachable only through a spelling the standard does not define. The grammar now reads `EDITING ( cobolWord | literal ) ...` and the quoted spelling draws the named COBOL2149 at bind rather than an ANTLR syntax error (parse-wide/bind-narrow, this grammar's stated discipline). MEASURED: PIC 99T99 EDITING T IS ":" compiles and renders 12:30; PIC 999 EDITING T IS ":" draws COBOL1593 naming SR10; PIC 99T99 EDITING "T" IS ":" draws COBOL2149.
